name: Helper Functions Demo
description: Showcase the pre-loaded helper functions: data loading, export, visualization, and utilities.

cells.code:
# Show current AWS identity and environment
info = whoami()

## 📦 Data Loading

Load data from local files, S3, DynamoDB, or URLs — all in one line.

# Load a built-in sample dataset
# Available: 'sales', 'customers', 'web_traffic', 'ab_test'
df = sample_data('sales')
print(f"Loaded {len(df)} rows")
df.head()

# Read CSV directly from S3 (uses the execution role — no credentials needed)
bucket = info['bucket']
sales = read_s3_csv(bucket, "samples/sales_data.csv")
print(f"Loaded {len(sales)} rows from S3")
sales.head()

# Read from DynamoDB (scans the table into a DataFrame)
dynamo_df = read_dynamodb("microvm-demo-data")
print(f"DynamoDB: {len(dynamo_df)} items")
dynamo_df.head()

# Fetch data from a public URL
iris = read_url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/iris.csv")
print(f"Iris dataset: {iris.shape}")
iris.head()

## 🔧 Utilities

Profile, compare, explore — all without boilerplate.

# Profile a DataFrame: types, nulls, unique values
profile(sales)

# List objects in an S3 bucket
files = list_s3(info['bucket'], "samples/")
files

# Preview first 5 rows from S3 without downloading the full file
preview = head_s3(info['bucket'], "samples/sales_data.csv", n=5)
preview

# Compare two DataFrames (useful for before/after cleaning)
# First compute revenue column
sales['revenue'] = sales['quantity'] * sales['unit_price'] * (1 - sales['discount'])

# Create a "cleaned" version by dropping nulls and adding a column
sales_clean = sales.dropna().copy()
sales_clean['revenue_rank'] = sales_clean['revenue'].rank(ascending=False)

compare_df(sales, sales_clean, "original", "cleaned")

## 📊 Visualization

One-liner interactive Plotly charts. All return the figure object for further customization.

# Interactive bar chart
product_rev = sales.groupby('product')['revenue'].sum().reset_index()
plot_bar(product_rev, x='product', y='revenue', title='Revenue by Product')

# Interactive scatter plot with size and color encoding
plot_scatter(sales, x='quantity', y='revenue', size='unit_price', color='product', title='Quantity vs Revenue')

# Interactive histogram
plot_histogram(sales, 'revenue', bins=25, title='Revenue Distribution')

# Heatmap from a pivot (product x region → revenue)
plot_heatmap(sales, x='region', y='product', value='revenue', title='Revenue: Product × Region')

## 💾 Data Export

Save results back to S3 or local files.

# Save to local file (auto-detects format from extension)
to_local(summary, '/tmp/sales_summary.csv')
to_local(summary, '/tmp/sales_summary.parquet')
print("Saved locally ✓")

# Upload to S3
uri = to_s3_csv(summary, info['bucket'], "user-data/sales_summary.csv")
print(f"Uploaded to: {uri}")

# Verify the upload
files = list_s3(info['bucket'], "user-data/")
files
